key.name: port-mutes
key.description: Stringified USB-C port numbers (the daemon's "port_number" int32 cast to a string) that should not raise CapabilityDegraded notifications. Written by the "Don't notify for this port again" notification action and by the per-row trash button in the preferences window. Read live on every CapabilityDegraded event by src/notifier.js.

key.name: data-rate-mutes
key.description: (device id, headline) pairs that should not raise DataRateDegraded notifications. The id is the daemon's "usb:<bus_port>" string — it is topological, so an entry means "this device on this port"; moving the device to a faster port changes the id and clears the condition anyway. The headline is stored so the preferences row can name the device instead of showing a bus path. Written by the "Don't notify for this device again" notification action and by the per-row trash button in the preferences window. Read live on every DataRateDegraded event by src/notifier.js.

key.name: hide-empty-ports
key.summary: Hide empty USB-C ports from the popover
key.description: When true, USB-C port rows whose status is "Empty" are not rendered in the tile popover. Toggled from the "Hide empty USB-C ports" switch in the preferences window. Read once per popover rebuild by src/popover.js populateDeviceRows.

key.name: show-hubs
key.summary: Show USB hub devices in the popover
key.description: When false (the default), USB hub devices are hidden from the tile popover. Toggled from the "Show USB Hubs" switch in the preferences window. Read once per popover rebuild by src/popover.js populateDeviceRows.

key.name: hide-builtin-devices
key.summary: Hide built-in (non-removable) USB devices from the popover
key.description: When true, USB devices the daemon reports as physically built into the machine are not rendered in the tile popover — the soldered-down webcam, fingerprint reader and Bluetooth radio are the usual members. The test is the daemon's "mount" property being the literal token "fixed", which usbeehive reads from the kernel's sysfs "removable" attribute and only ever emits as "fixed" or "removable". A device whose mount the kernel did not report is therefore never hidden: absence means "unknown", not "built in". A built-in device that currently carries an issue stays visible regardless, so the header's issue count can never name a row the user cannot reach — the same escape hatch show-hubs uses. Default false: hiding devices by default would silently omit hardware on first run, and this filter is additive to show-hubs rather than a replacement for it. Toggled from the "Hide built-in devices" switch in the preferences window and from the Options section of the popover. Read once per popover rebuild by src/popover.js populateDeviceRows.

key.name: show-technical-details
key.summary: Show technical detail rows in the device popover
key.description: When false (the default), the device detail panel shows only the glanceable property rows. Two groups are hidden: the curated advanced keys (serial, data role, cable details, drivers, port and connector identifiers, kernel workarounds, capability internals) and any key this build of USBee does not recognise — for example a newer usbeehive's additions. Unrecognised keys are never dropped and never raise an error; they are simply one toggle away. See src/property-policy.js for the full tiering, and quick task 260905-b0s for why this reversed the earlier "unknown keys are always visible" policy. Toggled from the "Show technical details" switch in the preferences window. Read once per popover rebuild by src/popover.js populateDeviceRows.

key.name: device-change-notify-scope
key.description: Controls whether DeviceAdded / DeviceRemoved D-Bus signals raise transient MessageTray toasts. "all" (the default) notifies on every device change. "power" restricts toasts to charging- relevant devices (TypeCPort category, or Phone / Storage device class). "off" suppresses device-change toasts entirely — this does NOT affect CapabilityDegraded notifications, which remain gated by port-mutes. Read live on every DeviceAdded / DeviceRemoved signal by src/notifier.js.
